Short answer
- If you terminate for convenience, you must give ninety days’ written notice (Section 3.2). Under Section 7.1, the Customer remains liable for fees accrued through the termination effective date. Practically that means you will owe any fees that have accrued up to the date the termination becomes effective (including fees for the 90‑day notice period), unless another provision in the MSA says otherwise.

Exact text you can quote in the memo
- Page 4, §3.2: "either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice."
- Page 11, §7.1: "termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date."

Limitations and recommended next step
- I only have the two excerpts you pasted. To be certain what counts as "fees" and exactly when the "effective date" is defined (and whether there are any additional early‑termination charges, minimum commitments, or invoicing rules), check the MSA definitions and the payment/termination sections (e.g., definitions of "Fees," "Effective Date," payment terms, and any other termination subsections). If you paste those sections or the full MSA I can give a definitive, citeable line-by-line draft for your memo.
